facts.text: Michigan City’s beaches hide a secret: the sand sings when you walk on it, earning the nickname “singing sand.”.
The city proudly hosts one of the nation’s oldest active municipal bands, a living reminder of its musical heritage.
A trip to Michigan City’s public library takes you back to 1897, when Marilla Waite Freeman opened the first doors of the Michigan City Public Library.
Michigan City sits right on Lake Michigan and borders Indiana Dunes National Park, making it a gateway to one of the country’s most celebrated dune landscapes.
Located about 45 miles east of Chicago, Michigan City links the Midwest to the Great Lakes through its historic South Shore Line train service.
Amtrak trains pass through Michigan City every day, but the nearest stop is ten miles away in New Buffalo, Michigan, a reminder of the city’s quiet rail history.
